name: Mehuman
overview: Mehuman was a male eunuch who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus, as one of seven eunuchs mentioned in the biblical book of Esther. Scripture does not specify his tribe or any additional personal details beyond his role in the royal court. His position as a eunuch indicates he held a trusted and significant office within the king's service.
namesAndTitles: The name Mehuman appears as a proper name in Esther 1:10. There is no recorded meaning or divine origin associated with this name in the biblical text, so it is presented plainly without additional significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Mehuman beyond his identification as one of the seven eunuchs serving King Ahasuerus. No other familial connections or relational details are provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Mehuman's significance lies in his role as a member of the king's eunuch officials, serving closely in the royal presence during the time of King Ahasuerus. Although he is mentioned briefly, his inclusion highlights the structure of the king's court and those who attended to royal duties. His service reflects the trusted positions held by eunuchs in the Persian administration as recorded in the book of Esther.
